answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may earn, like a reef that only grows where coral commits. The stake is time-locked and slashed when duplicate identities are proven, so an attacker must fund each fake identity separately: cost scales linearly while reward does not. Idle stake earns nothing, and reputation decays like a dune shifting in wind, so bought history cannot be hoarded. Honest agents recover their stake plus a nectar-like yield from real work, while sybils pay full price per copy and lose it on detection.
